   627→    p_list = subparsers.add_parser("list", help="List configs with key metadata")
   628→    p_list.add_argument("--dir", default=None, help="Directory containing YAML configs")
   629→    p_list.add_argument(
   630→        "--format",
   631→        choices=["table", "json"],
   632→        default="table",
   633→        help="Output format (default: table)",
   634→    )
   635→
   636→    # -- get --
   637→    p_get = subparsers.add_parser("get", help="Read a field value from configs")
   638→    p_get.add_argument("--field", required=True, help="Dotted path, e.g. llm.model")
   639→    p_get_source = p_get.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
   640→    p_get_source.add_argument("--config", default=None, help="Single config file")
   641→    p_get_source.add_argument("--dir", default=None, help="Directory of configs")
   642→    p_get.add_argument("--filter", default=None, help="Substring filter on filenames")
   643→
   644→    # -- set --
   645→    p_set = subparsers.add_parser("set", help="Update a field in configs")
   646→    p_set.add_argument("--field", required=True, help="Dotted path, e.g. llm.model")
   647→    p_set.add_argument("--value", required=True, help="New value (auto-coerced)")
   648→    p_set_source = p_set.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
   649→    p_set_source.add_argument("--config", default=None, help="Single config file")
   650→    p_set_source.add_argument("--dir", default=None, help="Directory of configs")
   651→    p_set.add_argument("--filter", default=None, help="Substring filter on filenames")
   652→    p_set.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Show changes without writing")
   653→
   654→    # -- clone --
   655→    p_clone = subparsers.add_parser("clone", help="Create a new config from a base")
   656→    p_clone.add_argument("--base", required=True, help="Path to the base config YAML")
   657→    p_clone.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True, help="Directory to write clone")
   658→    p_clone.add_argument("--model", default=None, help="Override llm.model and bdikit_models")
   659→    p_clone.add_argument("--provider", default=None, help="Override llm.provider")
   660→    p_clone.add_argument("--context", default=None, help="Override experiment.context")
   661→    p_clone.add_argument("--name", default=None, help="Custom experiment name slug")
   662→
   663→    # -- regenerate --
   664→    p_regen = subparsers.add_parser("regenerate", help="Rebuild associated .env for a config")
   665→    p_regen.add_argument("--config", required=True, help="Path to config YAML")
   666→
   667→    # -- validate --
   668→    p_validate = subparsers.add_parser("validate", help="Validate configs in a directory")
   669→    p_validate.add_argument("--dir", default=None, help="Directory containing YAML configs")
   670→
   671→    return parser
   672→
   673→
   674→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   675→# Main
   676→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   677→
   678→
   679→def main() -> int:
   680→    parser = build_parser()
   681→    args = parser.parse_args()
   682→
   683→    dispatch = {
   684→        "list": cmd_list,
   685→        "get": cmd_get,
   686→        "set": cmd_set,
   687→        "clone": cmd_clone,
   688→        "regenerate": cmd_regenerate,
   689→        "validate": cmd_validate,
   690→    }
   691→
   692→    handler = dispatch.get(args.command)
   693→    if handler is None:
   694→        parser.print_help()
   695→        return 2
   696→
   697→    return handler(args)
   698→
   699→
   700→if __name__ == "__main__":
   701→    sys.exit(main())

   100→
   101→        # Initialize tracing

   115→        self.is_running = False

   120→

   124→
   125→    async def start(self) -> None:
   126→        """
   127→        Start monitoring the Beaker session.
   128→

   130→        Call stop() or press Ctrl+C to end monitoring and save logs.
   131→        """

   139→            llm_model=self.config.llm.model,

   141→        )
   142→        # Attach config snapshot to trace
   143→        if hasattr(self.trace_logger, 'trace') and self.trace_logger.trace:

   163→
   164→        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
   165→        print("Manual Experiment Monitor Started")
   166→        print(f"{'='*60}")

   171→            print(f"Tracing: enabled ({self.config.tracing.phoenix_endpoint})")
   172→        print(f"{'='*60}")
   173→        print("\nMonitoring Beaker session... Press Ctrl+C to stop and save logs.\n")
   174→
   175→        # Open root tracing span (manual lifecycle since monitoring is open-ended)
   176→        if self.tracing_active and self.tracer:
   177→            self._root_span_ctx = experiment_span(
   178→                self.tracer, self.config, self.run_id,
   179→            )
   180→            self._root_span = self._root_span_ctx.__enter__()
   181→

   183→            await self._monitor_loop()
   184→        except asyncio.CancelledError:
   185→            pass
   186→        finally:

   188→            if self._root_span_ctx is not None:

   195→    async def _connect_to_kernel(self) -> None:
   196→        """Connect to existing Beaker kernel via WebSocket."""
   197→        # Wait for a session to be created (user needs to open browser first)
   198→        print("Waiting for Beaker session to be created...")
   199→        print("  \u2192 Open the Beaker URL in your browser to create a session")
   200→
   201→        sessions = []
   202→        wait_time = 0
   203→        max_wait = 3600  # Wait up to 1 hour for user to connect
   204→
   205→        while not sessions and wait_time < max_wait:
   206→            async with self.session.get(f"{self.server_url}/api/sessions") as resp:
   207→                if resp.status != 200:
   208→                    raise ConnectionError(f"Failed to get sessions: {resp.status}")
   209→                sessions = await resp.json()
   210→
   211→            if not sessions:
   212→                await asyncio.sleep(5)
   213→                wait_time += 5
   214→                if wait_time % 30 == 0:
   215→                    print(f"  Still waiting for session... ({wait_time}s)")
   216→
   217→        if not sessions:
   218→            raise ConnectionError(
   219→                "No active Beaker session found after timeout. "
   220→                "Make sure to open the Beaker URL in your browser."
   221→            )
   222→
   223→        # Use the first session
   224→        session = sessions[0]
   225→        self.kernel_id = session["kernel"]["id"]
   226→        session_id = session["id"]
   227→
   228→        # Connect WebSocket
   229→        ws_base = self.server_url.replace("http://", "ws://").replace("https://", "wss://")
   230→        ws_url = f"{ws_base}/api/kernels/{self.kernel_id}/channels?token={self.token}"
   231→
   232→        self.ws = await self.session.ws_connect(
   233→            ws_url,
   234→            timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=None),  # No timeout for monitoring
   235→        )
   236→
   237→        print(f"  Connected to kernel: {self.kernel_id}")
   238→        print(f"  Session: {session_id}")
   239→
   240→    async def _monitor_loop(self) -> None:
   241→        """Main loop to monitor WebSocket messages."""
   242→        while self.is_running:
   243→            try:
   244→                msg = await asyncio.wait_for(
   245→                    self.ws.receive_json(),
   246→                    timeout=1.0,  # Short timeout to check is_running flag
   247→                )
   248→                await self._handle_message(msg)
   249→            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
   250→                # No message received, continue monitoring
   251→                continue
   252→            except aiohttp.WSServerHandshakeError as e:
   253→                print(f"WebSocket error: {e}")
   254→                break
   255→
   256→    async def _handle_message(self, msg: dict) -> None:
   257→        """Handle a WebSocket message and log if relevant."""
   258→        msg_type = msg.get("msg_type", "")
   259→        content = msg.get("content", {})
   260→        header = msg.get("header", {})
   261→        parent_header = msg.get("parent_header", {})
   262→
   263→        msg_id = header.get("msg_id", "")
   264→        parent_msg_id = parent_header.get("msg_id", "")
   265→
   266→        # Track llm_request messages (user input)
   267→        if msg_type == "llm_request":
   268→            user_message = content.get("request", "")
   269→            self._pending_requests[msg_id] = {
   270→                "user_message": user_message,
   271→                "start_time": asyncio.get_event_loop().time(),
   272→                "raw_messages": [msg],
   273→                "tool_calls": [],
   274→            }
   275→            print(f"  [Turn {self.current_turn + 1}] User: {user_message[:80]}{'...' if len(user_message) > 80 else ''}")
   276→
   277→        # Track responses to pending requests
   278→        elif parent_msg_id in self._pending_requests:
   279→            pending = self._pending_requests[parent_msg_id]
   280→            pending["raw_messages"].append(msg)
   281→
   282→            if msg_type == "thought":
   283→                # Track tool calls from thoughts
   284→                thought = content.get("thought", "")
   285→                if "Action:" in thought:
   286→                    pending["tool_calls"].append({"thought": thought})
   287→
   288→            elif msg_type == "llm_response":
   289→                # Final LLM response - log the complete turn
   290→                self.current_turn += 1
   291→                agent_response = content.get("text", "")
   292→                duration = asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - pending["start_time"]
   293→
   294→                # Extract token usage and code executions
   295→                usage_records = extract_usage_records(pending["raw_messages"])
   296→                code_execs = extract_code_executions(pending["raw_messages"])
   297→                pricing_prompt = self.config.model_metadata.pricing_prompt_per_million_tokens
   298→                pricing_completion = self.config.model_metadata.pricing_completion_per_million_tokens
   299→                input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd = calculate_turn_cost(
   300→                    usage_records, pricing_prompt, pricing_completion
   301→                )
   302→
   303→                # Create tracing spans
   304→                if self.tracing_active and self.tracer:
   305→                    with turn_span(self.tracer, self.current_turn, pending["user_message"]) as tspan:
   306→                        for i, usage in enumerate(usage_records):
   307→                            with llm_call_span(self.tracer, i, self.config.llm.model) as lspan:
   308→                                set_llm_usage(lspan, usage, pricing_prompt, pricing_completion)
   309→                        for exec_data in code_execs:
   310→                            with tool_span(self.tracer, "beaker_execute", exec_data.get("code", "")) as ts:
   311→                                if ts is not None:
   312→                                    ts.set_attribute("output.value", exec_data.get("stdout", ""))
   313→                                    ts.set_attribute("tool.status", exec_data.get("status", "unknown"))
   314→                        if tspan is not None:
   315→                            tspan.set_attribute("output.value", agent_response)
   316→                            tspan.set_attribute("harmonia.duration_seconds", duration)
   317→
   318→                self.trace_logger.log_turn(
   319→                    turn=self.current_turn,
   320→                    user_message=pending["user_message"],
   321→                    agent_response=agent_response,
   322→                    response_type="llm_response",
   323→                    tool_calls=pending["tool_calls"],
   324→                    duration_seconds=duration,
   325→                    raw_messages=pending["raw_messages"],
   326→                    input_tokens=input_tokens,
   327→                    output_tokens=output_tokens,
   328→                    cost_usd=cost_usd,
   329→                    code_executions=code_execs,
   330→                    usage_records=usage_records,
   331→                )
   332→                self.conversation_logger.log_turn(
   333→                    turn=self.current_turn,
   334→                    user_message=pending["user_message"],
   335→                    agent_response=agent_response,
   336→                    response_type="llm_response",
   337→                )
   338→
   339→                # Auto-save after each turn
   340→                self._save_intermediate()
   341→
   342→                print(f"  [Turn {self.current_turn}] Agent: {agent_response[:80]}{'...' if len(agent_response) > 80 else ''}")
   343→
   344→                # Clean up
   345→                del self._pending_requests[parent_msg_id]
   346→
   347→            elif msg_type == "code_cell":
   348→                # Code cell response
   349→                self.current_turn += 1
   350→                code = content.get("code", "")
   351→                duration = asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - pending["start_time"]
   352→
   353→                # Extract token usage and code executions
   354→                usage_records = extract_usage_records(pending["raw_messages"])
   355→                code_execs = extract_code_executions(pending["raw_messages"])
   356→                pricing_prompt = self.config.model_metadata.pricing_prompt_per_million_tokens
   357→                pricing_completion = self.config.model_metadata.pricing_completion_per_million_tokens
   358→                input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd = calculate_turn_cost(
   359→                    usage_records, pricing_prompt, pricing_completion
   360→                )
   361→
   362→                # Create tracing spans
   363→                if self.tracing_active and self.tracer:
   364→                    with turn_span(self.tracer, self.current_turn, pending["user_message"]) as tspan:
   365→                        for i, usage in enumerate(usage_records):
   366→                            with llm_call_span(self.tracer, i, self.config.llm.model) as lspan:
   367→                                set_llm_usage(lspan, usage, pricing_prompt, pricing_completion)
   368→                        if tspan is not None:
   369→                            tspan.set_attribute("output.value", code)
   370→                            tspan.set_attribute("harmonia.response_type", "code_cell")
   371→                            tspan.set_attribute("harmonia.duration_seconds", duration)
   372→
   373→                self.trace_logger.log_turn(
   374→                    turn=self.current_turn,
   375→                    user_message=pending["user_message"],
   376→                    agent_response=code,
   377→                    response_type="code_cell",
   378→                    tool_calls=pending["tool_calls"],
   379→                    duration_seconds=duration,
   380→                    raw_messages=pending["raw_messages"],
   381→                    input_tokens=input_tokens,
   382→                    output_tokens=output_tokens,
   383→                    cost_usd=cost_usd,
   384→                    code_executions=code_execs,
   385→                    usage_records=usage_records,
   386→                )
   387→                self.conversation_logger.log_turn(
   388→                    turn=self.current_turn,
   389→                    user_message=pending["user_message"],
   390→                    agent_response=f"```python\n{code}\n```",
   391→                    response_type="code_cell",
   392→                )
   393→
   394→                self._save_intermediate()
   395→                print(f"  [Turn {self.current_turn}] Agent: [code_cell] {code[:60]}{'...' if len(code) > 60 else ''}")
   396→
   397→                del self._pending_requests[parent_msg_id]
   398→
   399→            elif msg_type == "error":
   400→                # Error response
   401→                self.current_turn += 1
   402→                traceback = "\n".join(content.get("traceback", []))
   403→                duration = asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - pending["start_time"]
   404→
   405→                self.trace_logger.log_turn(
   406→                    turn=self.current_turn,
   407→                    user_message=pending["user_message"],
   408→                    agent_response=traceback,
   409→                    response_type="error",
   410→                    tool_calls=pending["tool_calls"],
   411→                    duration_seconds=duration,
   412→                    raw_messages=pending["raw_messages"],
   413→                )
   414→                self.conversation_logger.log_turn(
   415→                    turn=self.current_turn,
   416→                    user_message=pending["user_message"],
   417→                    agent_response=f"```\n{traceback}\n```",
   418→                    response_type="error",
   419→                )
   420→
   421→                self._save_intermediate()
   422→                print(f"  [Turn {self.current_turn}] Agent: [error] {content.get('ename', 'Error')}")
   423→
   424→                del self._pending_requests[parent_msg_id]
   425→
   426→    def _save_intermediate(self) -> None:
   427→        """Save intermediate results (in case of crash or early termination)."""
   428→        try:
   429→            # Update end time and save
   430→            if self.trace_logger.trace:
   431→                self.trace_logger.trace.end_time = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
   432→                total = sum(t.duration_seconds for t in self.trace_logger.trace.turns)
   433→                self.trace_logger.trace.total_duration_seconds = total
   434→                self.trace_logger.trace.status = "running"
   435→            self.trace_logger.save()
   436→            self.conversation_logger.save()
   437→        except Exception as e:
   438→            print(f"  Warning: Failed to save intermediate results: {e}")
   439→
   440→    async def _finalize(self) -> None:
   441→        """Finalize logging and close connections."""
   442→        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
   443→        print("Stopping monitor and saving logs...")
   444→
   445→        # End experiment
   446→        self.trace_logger.end_experiment(status="completed")
   447→        self.conversation_logger.log_summary(
   448→            total_turns=self.current_turn,
   449→            total_duration=self.trace_logger.trace.total_duration_seconds if self.trace_logger.trace else 0,
   450→            status="completed",
   451→        )
   452→
   453→        # Save final logs
   454→        trace_path = self.trace_logger.save()
   455→        conv_path = self.conversation_logger.save()
   456→
   457→        print("\nExperiment complete!")
   458→        print(f"  Total turns: {self.current_turn}")
   459→        print(f"  Output directory: {self.output_dir}")
   460→        print(f"  - {trace_path.name}")
   461→        print(f"  - {conv_path.name}")
   462→        print(f"{'='*60}\n")
   463→
   464→        # Close connections
   465→        if self.ws and not self.ws.closed:
   466→            await self.ws.close()
   467→        if self.session:
   468→            await self.session.close()
   469→
   470→    def stop(self) -> None:
   471→        """Stop monitoring."""
   472→        self.is_running = False

   475→async def run_manual_experiment(
   476→    config_path: Path,
   477→    server_url: str = "http://localhost:8100",
   478→    token: Optional[str] = None,
   479→    output_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
   480→) -> Path:
   481→    """
   482→    Run a manual experiment with logging.
   483→
   484→    Args:
   485→        config_path: Path to experiment configuration YAML
   486→        server_url: Beaker server URL
   487→        token: Jupyter authentication token
   488→        output_dir: Override output directory
   489→
   490→    Returns:
   491→        Path to output directory with logs
   492→    """
   493→    import os
   494→
   495→    # Load config
   496→    config = load_config(config_path)
   497→
   498→    # Get token from environment if not provided
   499→    if not token:
   500→        token = os.environ.get("JUPYTER_TOKEN")
   501→    if not token:
   502→        raise ValueError("No token provided. Set JUPYTER_TOKEN or pass --token")
   503→
   504→    # Create runner
   505→    runner = ManualExperimentRunner(
   506→        server_url=server_url,
   507→        token=token,
   508→        config=config,
   509→        output_dir=output_dir,
   510→    )
   511→
   512→    # Set up signal handlers for graceful shutdown
   513→    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
   514→
   515→    def signal_handler():
   516→        print("\n\nReceived interrupt signal...")
   517→        runner.stop()
   518→
   519→    for sig in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
   520→        loop.add_signal_handler(sig, signal_handler)
   521→
   522→    # Run
   523→    await runner.start()
   524→
   525→    return runner.output_dir

     4→Outer-joins on run_id so runs are visible even if one source is missing.
     5→"""

     8→import logging
     9→import re
    10→import threading
    11→from pathlib import Path
    12→from typing import Optional
    13→
    14→import pandas as pd
    15→import yaml
    16→from evaluation.visualization.io import (
    17→    RUN_ID_PATTERN,
    18→)
    19→
    20→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    21→
    22→try:
    23→    from openinference.semconv.trace import SpanAttributes
    24→    _OPENINFERENCE_AVAILABLE = True
    25→except ImportError:
    26→    _OPENINFERENCE_AVAILABLE = False
    27→
    28→try:
    29→    import phoenix as px
    30→    _PHOENIX_AVAILABLE = True
    31→except ImportError:
    32→    _PHOENIX_AVAILABLE = False
    33→
    34→# Regex to distinguish SLURM job ID (all digits) from timestamp (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS)
    35→_SLURM_JOB_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+$")
    36→_TIMESTAMP_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{8}_\d{6}$")
    37→
    38→# Expected metrics schema version
    39→_EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.1"

    41→
    42→class DashboardDataLoader:
    43→    """Loads experiment data from results directories and optionally Phoenix."""
    44→
    45→    def __init__(self, phoenix_endpoint: str, results_base_dir: Path):
    46→        self.phoenix_endpoint = phoenix_endpoint
    47→        self.results_dir = Path(results_base_dir)
    48→        self._phoenix_client = None
    49→        self._phoenix_available = False
    50→        self._cache_lock = threading.Lock()
    51→        self._run_index: dict[str, Path] = {}  # run_id -> canonical results dir
    52→        self._metrics_cache: dict[str, dict] = {}
    53→        self._trace_cache: dict[str, dict] = {}
    54→
    55→        self._init_phoenix()
    56→        self._build_run_index()
    57→
    58→    def _init_phoenix(self):
    59→        """Try to connect to Phoenix. Set _phoenix_available flag."""
    60→        if not _PHOENIX_AVAILABLE:
    61→            return
    62→        try:
    63→            self._phoenix_client = px.Client(endpoint=self.phoenix_endpoint)
    64→            self._phoenix_client.get_spans_dataframe(limit=1)
    65→            self._phoenix_available = True
    66→        except Exception:
    67→            self._phoenix_available = False
    68→            self._phoenix_client = None
    69→
    70→    def _build_run_index(self):
    71→        """
    72→        Scan results/ directory names to build run_id -> directory mapping.
    73→        When a run_id maps to multiple directories, prefer the SLURM-job-ID
    74→        format (shorter middle segment) as canonical.
    75→        """
    76→        if not self.results_dir.is_dir():
    77→            return
    78→
    79→        # Collect all candidate dirs per run_id
    80→        candidates: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}
    81→        for d in sorted(self.results_dir.iterdir()):
    82→            if not d.is_dir():
    83→                continue
    84→            m = RUN_ID_PATTERN.search(d.name)
    85→            if m:
    86→                rid = m.group(1)
    87→                candidates.setdefault(rid, []).append(d)
    88→
    89→        with self._cache_lock:
    90→            for rid, dirs in candidates.items():
    91→                if len(dirs) == 1:
    92→                    self._run_index[rid] = dirs[0]
    93→                else:
    94→                    # Prefer SLURM format: {name}_{job_id}_{run_id}
    95→                    # The segment before run_id in SLURM format is all digits
    96→                    best = dirs[0]
    97→                    for d in dirs:
    98→                        # Remove the run_id suffix, check preceding segment
    99→                        prefix = d.name[: -(len(rid) + 1)]  # remove _<run_id>
   100→                        parts = prefix.rsplit("_", 1)
   101→                        if len(parts) == 2 and _SLURM_JOB_ID_RE.match(parts[1]):
   102→                            best = d
   103→                            break
   104→                    self._run_index[rid] = best
   105→
   106→    def _parse_dir_metadata(self, run_id: str, d: Path) -> dict:
   107→        """Extract metadata from a results directory without loading large files."""
   108→        meta = {
   109→            "run_id": run_id,
   110→            "results_dir": str(d),
   111→            "has_metrics": (d / "metrics.json").exists(),
   112→            "has_trace": (d / "trace.json").exists(),
   113→            "has_config": (d / "config_snapshot.yaml").exists(),
   114→        }
   115→
   116→        # Try to get basic info from trace.json (lightweight: read top-level keys only)
   117→        if meta["has_trace"]:
   118→            try:
   119→                with open(d / "trace.json") as f:
   120→                    trace_data = json.load(f)
   121→                meta["experiment_name"] = trace_data.get("experiment", {}).get("name", "")
   122→                meta["model"] = trace_data.get("llm", {}).get("model", "")
   123→                meta["provider"] = trace_data.get("llm", {}).get("provider", "")
   124→                meta["status"] = trace_data.get("status", "unknown")
   125→                meta["total_turns"] = len(trace_data.get("turns", []))
   126→                meta["total_duration"] = trace_data.get("timing", {}).get("total_duration_seconds", 0)
   127→                timing = trace_data.get("timing", {})
   128→                meta["start_time"] = timing.get("start_time", "")
   129→
   130→                # Sum token/cost from turns
   131→                turns = trace_data.get("turns", [])
   132→                meta["total_input_tokens"] = sum(t.get("input_tokens", 0) for t in turns)
   133→                meta["total_output_tokens"] = sum(t.get("output_tokens", 0) for t in turns)
   134→                meta["total_cost_usd"] = sum(t.get("cost_usd", 0) for t in turns)
   135→            except Exception:
   136→                pass
   137→
   138→        # Try to get accuracy from metrics.json (small file)
   139→        if meta["has_metrics"]:
   140→            try:
   141→                metrics = self.get_run_metrics(run_id)
   142→                if metrics:
   143→                    meta["accuracy"] = metrics.get("overall_summary", {}).get("avg_accuracy_excl_empty")
   144→                    meta["column_mapping_accuracy"] = metrics.get("column_mapping", {}).get("accuracy")
   145→                    md = metrics.get("metadata", {})
   146→                    # Fill in model/provider from metrics if not from trace
   147→                    if not meta.get("model"):
   148→                        meta["model"] = md.get("llm_model", "")
   149→                    if not meta.get("provider"):
   150→                        meta["provider"] = md.get("llm_provider", "")
   151→                    if not meta.get("experiment_name"):
   152→                        meta["experiment_name"] = md.get("experiment_name", "")
   153→            except Exception:
   154→                pass
   155→
   156→        # Fill defaults for missing fields
   157→        meta.setdefault("experiment_name", d.name)
   158→        meta.setdefault("model", "")
   159→        meta.setdefault("provider", "")
   160→        meta.setdefault("status", "unknown")
   161→        meta.setdefault("total_turns", 0)
   162→        meta.setdefault("total_duration", 0)
   163→        meta.setdefault("total_input_tokens", 0)
   164→        meta.setdefault("total_output_tokens", 0)
   165→        meta.setdefault("total_cost_usd", 0)
   166→        meta.setdefault("start_time", "")
   167→        meta.setdefault("accuracy", None)
   168→        meta.setdefault("column_mapping_accuracy", None)
   169→
   170→        return meta

   172→    def get_all_runs(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
   173→        """
   174→        Dual-source run discovery.
   175→        Returns DataFrame with run metadata.
   176→        """
   177→        rows = []
   178→
   179→        # Source 1: File-based discovery
   180→        with self._cache_lock:
   181→            index_copy = dict(self._run_index)
   182→        for run_id, d in index_copy.items():
   183→            meta = self._parse_dir_metadata(run_id, d)
   184→            meta["has_phoenix_data"] = False
   185→            rows.append(meta)
   186→
   187→        # Source 2: Phoenix spans (if available)
   188→        if self._phoenix_available and self._phoenix_client:
   189→            try:
   190→                spans_df = self._phoenix_client.get_spans_dataframe()
   191→                if spans_df is not None and len(spans_df) > 0:
   192→                    # Find root AGENT spans with harmonia.run_id
   193→                    rid_col = "attributes.harmonia.run_id"
   194→                    if rid_col in spans_df.columns:
   195→                        root_spans = spans_df[spans_df[rid_col].notna()].copy()
   196→                        phoenix_run_ids = set(root_spans[rid_col].unique())
   197→
   198→                        # Mark existing runs as having Phoenix data
   199→                        existing_ids = {r["run_id"] for r in rows}
   200→                        for row in rows:
   201→                            if row["run_id"] in phoenix_run_ids:
   202→                                row["has_phoenix_data"] = True
   203→
   204→                        # Add Phoenix-only runs (no local files)
   205→                        for rid in phoenix_run_ids - existing_ids:
   206→                            span = root_spans[root_spans[rid_col] == rid].iloc[0]
   207→                            meta = {
   208→                                "run_id": rid,
   209→                                "results_dir": "",
   210→                                "has_metrics": False,
   211→                                "has_trace": False,
   212→                                "has_config": False,
   213→                                "has_phoenix_data": True,
   214→                                "experiment_name": span.get("attributes.harmonia.experiment_name", ""),
   215→                                "model": span.get(f"attributes.{SpanAttributes.LLM_MODEL_NAME}", "") if _OPENINFERENCE_AVAILABLE else span.get("attributes.llm.model_name", ""),
   216→                                "provider": span.get("attributes.harmonia.llm_provider", ""),
   217→                                "status": "unknown",
   218→                                "total_turns": 0,
   219→                                "total_duration": 0,
   220→                                "total_input_tokens": 0,
   221→                                "total_output_tokens": 0,
   222→                                "total_cost_usd": 0,
   223→                                "start_time": "",
   224→                                "accuracy": None,
   225→                                "column_mapping_accuracy": None,
   226→                            }
   227→                            rows.append(meta)
   228→            except Exception as e:
   229→                logger.warning(f"Error querying Phoenix: {e}")
   230→
   231→        if not rows:
   232→            return pd.DataFrame(columns=[
   233→                "run_id", "experiment_name", "model", "provider", "status",
   234→                "total_turns", "total_duration", "total_input_tokens",
   235→                "total_output_tokens", "total_cost_usd", "start_time",
   236→                "accuracy", "column_mapping_accuracy",
   237→                "has_metrics", "has_trace", "has_config", "has_phoenix_data",
   238→                "results_dir",
   239→            ])
   240→
   241→        return pd.DataFrame(rows)

   243→    def get_run_spans(self, run_id: str) -> Optional[pd.DataFrame]:
   244→        """Get all spans for a specific run from Phoenix. Returns None if Phoenix unavailable."""
   245→        if not self._phoenix_available or not self._phoenix_client:
   246→            return None
   247→        try:
   248→            spans_df = self._phoenix_client.get_spans_dataframe()
   249→            if spans_df is None or len(spans_df) == 0:
   250→                return None
   251→            rid_col = "attributes.harmonia.run_id"
   252→            if rid_col not in spans_df.columns:
   253→                return None
   254→            run_spans = spans_df[spans_df[rid_col] == run_id]
   255→            return run_spans if len(run_spans) > 0 else None
   256→        except Exception:
   257→            return None

   259→    def get_run_metrics(self, run_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
   260→        """Load metrics.json for a run from its results directory."""
   261→        with self._cache_lock:
   262→            if run_id in self._metrics_cache:
   263→                return self._metrics_cache[run_id]
   264→
   265→        d = self.find_results_dir(run_id)
   266→        if d is None:
   267→            return None
   268→
   269→        metrics_path = d / "metrics.json"
   270→        if not metrics_path.exists():
   271→            return None
   272→
   273→        try:
   274→            data = json.loads(metrics_path.read_text())
   275→            # Schema version check
   276→            sv = data.get("schema_version", "")
   277→            if sv and sv != _EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION:
   278→                logger.warning(
   279→                    f"metrics.json for run {run_id} has schema_version={sv} "
   280→                    f"(expected {_EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION}). Loading best-effort."
   281→                )
   282→            with self._cache_lock:
   283→                self._metrics_cache[run_id] = data
   284→            return data
   285→        except Exception as e:
   286→            logger.warning(f"Error loading metrics for run {run_id}: {e}")
   287→            return None

   289→    def get_run_trace(self, run_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
   290→        """Load trace.json for a run from its results directory. Lazily loaded."""
   291→        with self._cache_lock:
   292→            if run_id in self._trace_cache:
   293→                return self._trace_cache[run_id]
   294→
   295→        d = self.find_results_dir(run_id)

   297→            return None
   298→
   299→        trace_path = d / "trace.json"
   300→        if not trace_path.exists():
   301→            return None
   302→
   303→        try:
   304→            data = json.loads(trace_path.read_text())
   305→            with self._cache_lock:
   306→                self._trace_cache[run_id] = data
   307→            return data
   308→        except Exception as e:

   312→    def get_run_config(self, run_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
   313→        """Load config_snapshot.yaml for a run. Returns None if missing."""
   314→        d = self.find_results_dir(run_id)

   318→        config_path = d / "config_snapshot.yaml"

   328→    def get_all_metrics(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
   329→        """
   330→        Aggregate metrics across all runs into a DataFrame.
   331→        One row per run with key metrics columns.
   332→        """
   333→        rows = []
   334→        with self._cache_lock:
   335→            index_copy = dict(self._run_index)
   336→
   337→        for run_id, d in index_copy.items():
   338→            metrics = self.get_run_metrics(run_id)
   339→            if metrics is None:
   340→                continue
   341→
   342→            md = metrics.get("metadata", {})
   343→            cm = metrics.get("column_mapping", {})
   344→            os_ = metrics.get("overall_summary", {})
   345→
   346→            # Get token/cost from trace if available
   347→            trace = self.get_run_trace(run_id)
   348→            total_input = 0
   349→            total_output = 0
   350→            total_cost = 0.0
   351→            total_turns = 0
   352→            if trace:
   353→                turns = trace.get("turns", [])
   354→                total_turns = len(turns)
   355→                total_input = sum(t.get("input_tokens", 0) for t in turns)
   356→                total_output = sum(t.get("output_tokens", 0) for t in turns)
   357→                total_cost = sum(t.get("cost_usd", 0) for t in turns)
   358→
   359→            rows.append({
   360→                "run_id": run_id,
   361→                "experiment_name": md.get("experiment_name", ""),
   362→                "model": md.get("llm_model", ""),
   363→                "provider": md.get("llm_provider", ""),
   364→                "model_family": md.get("model_family_group", ""),

     3→import json
     4→import re
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→RUN_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"_([0-9a-f]{8})$")
     9→
    10→
    11→def discover_metrics_files(metrics_files: list[str] | None = None, metrics_globs: list[str] | None = None) -> list[Path]:
    12→    paths: set[Path] = set()
    13→    for item in metrics_files or []:
    14→        p = Path(item).expanduser()
    15→        if p.is_file() and p.name == "metrics.json":
    16→            paths.add(p.resolve())
    17→        elif p.is_dir():
    18→            candidate = p / "metrics.json"
    19→            if candidate.exists():
    20→                paths.add(candidate.resolve())
    21→    for pattern in metrics_globs or []:
    22→        for p in Path().glob(pattern):
    23→            if p.is_file() and p.name == "metrics.json":
    24→                paths.add(p.resolve())
    25→    return sorted(paths)
    26→
    27→
    28→def extract_run_id(path: Path, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    29→    experiment_name = data.get("metadata", {}).get("experiment_name", "")
    30→    m = RUN_ID_PATTERN.search(experiment_name)
    31→    if m:
    32→        return m.group(1)
    33→    parent = path.parent.name
    34→    m = RUN_ID_PATTERN.search(parent)
    35→    return m.group(1) if m else parent
    36→
    37→
    38→def load_metrics_bundle(paths: list[Path]) -> tuple[list[tuple[Path, dict[str, Any]]], list[dict[str, str]]]:
    39→    loaded: list[tuple[Path, dict[str, Any]]] = []
    40→    skipped: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    41→    for path in paths:
    42→        try:
    43→            data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    44→            if "column_mapping" not in data or "column_values" not in data or "overall_summary" not in data:
    45→                skipped.append({"file": str(path), "reason": "missing required keys"})
    46→                continue
    47→            loaded.append((path, data))
    48→        except Exception as exc:
    49→            skipped.append({"file": str(path), "reason": str(exc)})
    50→    return loaded, skipped
    51→

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→CLI script for calculating metadata harmonization metrics.
     4→
     5→Compares LLM-produced harmonized output against gold standard data and produces
     6→a comprehensive metrics.json file with schema mapping quality, value harmonization
     7→quality, and error analysis.
     8→
     9→Usage:
    10→    python calculate_metrics.py --results-dir <path> [options]
    11→"""
    12→
    13→import argparse
    14→import csv
    15→import json
    16→import logging
    17→import sys
    18→from pathlib import Path
    19→from typing import Optional
    20→
    21→import yaml
    22→
    23→# Add src to path for imports
    24→sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent / "src"))
    25→
    26→from evaluation.metrics import calculate_all_metrics
    27→from evaluation.schemas import MetricsResult
    28→
    29→
    30→def setup_logging(verbose: bool, log_file: Optional[Path] = None) -> None:
    31→    """Setup logging configuration."""
    32→    level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO
    33→    format_str = "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"
    34→
    35→    handlers = [logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)]
    36→
    37→    if log_file:
    38→        handlers.append(logging.FileHandler(log_file))
    39→
    40→    logging.basicConfig(
    41→        level=level,
    42→        format=format_str,
    43→        handlers=handlers,
    44→    )
    45→
    46→
    47→def load_json(path: Path) -> dict | None:
    48→    """Load JSON file, return None if not found."""
    49→    if not path.exists():
    50→        return None
    51→    return json.loads(path.read_text())
    52→
    53→
    54→def load_yaml(path: Path) -> dict:
    55→    """Load YAML config file."""
    56→    with open(path, "r") as f:
    57→        return yaml.safe_load(f)
    58→
    59→
    60→def _write_row_values_csv(result, row_values_path: Path) -> None:
    61→    """Write row_values.csv from a MetricsResult."""
    62→    with open(row_values_path, "w", newline="") as f:
    63→        writer = csv.writer(f)
    64→        writer.writerow([
    65→            "column_name", "source_column_name", "row_index",
    66→            "gold_value", "predicted_value", "classification", "error_type",
    67→        ])
    68→        for col_name, col_metrics in result.column_values.items():
    69→            for rc in col_metrics.row_comparisons:
    70→                writer.writerow([
    71→                    col_name,
    72→                    col_metrics.source_column_name,
    73→                    rc.row_index,
    74→                    rc.gold_value,
    75→                    rc.predicted_value,
    76→                    rc.classification,
    77→                    rc.error_type or "",
    78→                ])
    79→
    80→
    81→def backfill_row_values(results_dir: Path, verbose: bool = False) -> int:
    82→    """Regenerate row_values.csv for an existing run without overwriting metrics.json.
    83→
    84→    Tries two strategies to find required paths:
    85→    1. From .experiment_id → config YAML → evaluation block
    86→    2. From metrics.json → gold_standard_file, llm_output_file (with gold_column_mapping
    87→       inferred from the gold standard directory)
    88→    """
    89→    setup_logging(verbose)
    90→    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    91→
    92→    results_dir = Path(results_dir)
    93→    row_values_path = results_dir / "row_values.csv"
    94→
    95→    gold_standard_path = None
    96→    gold_column_mapping_path = None
    97→    index_column = None
    98→    numeric_tolerance = None
    99→    acceptable_columns_path = None
   100→
   101→    # Strategy 1: .experiment_id → config YAML (check .runtime/ first, then old location)
   102→    exp_id_file = results_dir / ".runtime" / ".experiment_id"
   103→    if not exp_id_file.exists():
   104→        exp_id_file = results_dir / ".experiment_id"
   105→    if exp_id_file.exists():
   106→        exp_id = json.loads(exp_id_file.read_text())
   107→        config_path = exp_id.get("config_path")
   108→        if config_path:
   109→            config_path = Path(config_path)
   110→            if not config_path.is_absolute():
   111→                config_path = Path(__file__).parent / config_path
   112→            if config_path.exists():
   113→                config_data = load_yaml(config_path)
   114→                evaluation_config = config_data.get("evaluation", {})
   115→                gold_standard_path = evaluation_config.get("gold_standard")
   116→                gold_column_mapping_path = evaluation_config.get("gold_column_mapping")
   117→                index_column = evaluation_config.get("index_column")
   118→                numeric_tolerance = evaluation_config.get("numeric_tolerance")
   119→                acceptable_columns_path = evaluation_config.get("acceptable_columns_file")
   120→
   121→    # Strategy 2: fall back to metrics.json
   122→    if not gold_standard_path or not gold_column_mapping_path:
   123→        metrics_file = results_dir / "metrics.json"
   124→        if not metrics_file.exists():
   125→            logger.error(f"Neither .experiment_id config nor metrics.json found in {results_dir}")
   126→            return 1
   127→
   128→        metrics_data = json.loads(metrics_file.read_text())
   129→        gold_standard_path = gold_standard_path or metrics_data.get("gold_standard_file")
   130→
   131→        if gold_standard_path and not gold_column_mapping_path:
   132→            # Infer gold_column_mapping from gold standard directory
   133→            gs_dir = Path(gold_standard_path).parent
   134→            candidate = gs_dir / "gold_standard_column_mapping.json"
   135→            if candidate.exists():
   136→                gold_column_mapping_path = str(candidate)
   137→
   138→            if not gold_column_mapping_path:
   139→                # Try acceptable_columns as fallback for column list
   140→                candidate2 = gs_dir / "harmonization_acceptable_columns.json"
   141→                if candidate2.exists():
   142→                    acceptable_columns_path = str(candidate2)
   143→
   144→    if not gold_standard_path or not gold_column_mapping_path:
   145→        logger.error(f"Cannot determine gold_standard and gold_column_mapping for {results_dir}")
   146→        return 1
   147→
   148→    gold_standard_path = Path(gold_standard_path)
   149→    gold_column_mapping_path = Path(gold_column_mapping_path)
   150→
   151→    if not gold_standard_path.exists():
   152→        logger.error(f"Gold standard CSV not found: {gold_standard_path}")
   153→        return 1
   154→    if not gold_column_mapping_path.exists():
   155→        logger.error(f"Gold column mapping not found: {gold_column_mapping_path}")
   156→        return 1
   157→
   158→    # Find LLM output
   159→    llm_output_csv = results_dir / "dou_harmonized.csv"
   160→    if not llm_output_csv.exists():
   161→        candidates = list(results_dir.glob("*harmonized*.csv"))
   162→        if candidates:
   163→            llm_output_csv = candidates[0]
   164→        else:
   165→            logger.error(f"No harmonized output CSV found in {results_dir}")
   166→            return 1
   167→
   168→    # Load mappings
   169→    gold_column_mapping = load_json(gold_column_mapping_path)
   170→    llm_column_mapping = None
   171→    llm_column_mapping_file = results_dir / "column_mapping.json"
   172→    if llm_column_mapping_file.exists():
   173→        llm_column_mapping = load_json(llm_column_mapping_file)
   174→
   175→    acceptable_columns = None
   176→    if acceptable_columns_path:
   177→        acceptable_columns_path = Path(acceptable_columns_path)
   178→        if acceptable_columns_path.exists():
   179→            acceptable_columns = load_json(acceptable_columns_path)
   180→
   181→    logger.info(f"Backfilling row_values.csv for {results_dir.name}")
   182→
   183→    result = calculate_all_metrics(
   184→        gold_standard_csv=gold_standard_path,
   185→        llm_output_csv=llm_output_csv,
   186→        gold_column_mapping=gold_column_mapping,
   187→        llm_column_mapping=llm_column_mapping,
   188→        acceptable_columns=acceptable_columns,
   189→        index_column=index_column,
   190→        numeric_tolerance=numeric_tolerance,
   191→    )
   192→
   193→    _write_row_values_csv(result, row_values_path)
   194→    logger.info(f"✓ Row values backfilled to: {row_values_path}")
   195→    return 0
   196→
   197→
   198→def main():
   199→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   200→        description="Calculate metadata harmonization metrics",
   201→        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
   202→    )
   203→
   204→    # Required
   205→    parser.add_argument(
   206→        "--results-dir",
   207→        type=Path,
   208→        required=True,
   209→        help="Directory containing experiment results (with dou_harmonized.csv, etc.)",
   210→    )
   211→
   212→    # Config-based options
   213→    parser.add_argument(
   214→        "--config",
   215→        type=Path,
   216→        help="Experiment config YAML (reads evaluation block for paths)",
   217→    )
   218→
   219→    # Override options
   220→    parser.add_argument(
   221→        "--gold-standard",
   222→        type=Path,
   223→        help="Path to gold standard harmonized CSV",
   224→    )
   225→    parser.add_argument(
   226→        "--gold-column-mapping",
   227→        type=Path,
   228→        help="Path to gold standard column mapping JSON",
   229→    )
   230→    parser.add_argument(
   231→        "--gold-value-mapping",
   232→        type=Path,
   233→        help="Path to gold standard value mapping JSON (for reference)",
   234→    )
   235→    parser.add_argument(
   236→        "--acceptable-columns",
   237→        type=Path,
   238→        help="Path to acceptable alternative column mappings JSON",
   239→    )
   240→    parser.add_argument(

    70→    def _build_run_index(self):
    71→        """
    72→        Scan results/ directory names to build run_id -> directory mapping.
    73→        When a run_id maps to multiple directories, prefer the SLURM-job-ID
    74→        format (shorter middle segment) as canonical.
    75→        """
    76→        if not self.results_dir.is_dir():
    77→            return
    78→
    79→        # Collect all candidate dirs per run_id
    80→        candidates: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}
    81→        for d in sorted(self.results_dir.iterdir()):
    82→            if not d.is_dir():
    83→                continue
    84→            m = RUN_ID_PATTERN.search(d.name)
    85→            if m:
    86→                rid = m.group(1)
    87→                candidates.setdefault(rid, []).append(d)
    88→
    89→        with self._cache_lock:
    90→            for rid, dirs in candidates.items():
    91→                if len(dirs) == 1:
    92→                    self._run_index[rid] = dirs[0]
    93→                else:
    94→                    # Prefer SLURM format: {name}_{job_id}_{run_id}
    95→                    # The segment before run_id in SLURM format is all digits
    96→                    best = dirs[0]
    97→                    for d in dirs:
    98→                        # Remove the run_id suffix, check preceding segment
    99→                        prefix = d.name[: -(len(rid) + 1)]  # remove _<run_id>
   100→                        parts = prefix.rsplit("_", 1)
   101→                        if len(parts) == 2 and _SLURM_JOB_ID_RE.match(parts[1]):
   102→                            best = d
   103→                            break
   104→                    self._run_index[rid] = best

    fi

    echo "ERROR: Server failed to start within $MAX_WAIT seconds"

    --config {{config_path}} \
    --server http://localhost:$PORT \
    --token "$TOKEN" \

if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]; then

def plot_failure_distribution(
    all_runs_df: pd.DataFrame,
    backend: str = "seaborn",
    title: str | None = None,
):
    """Horizontal bar chart of failure reason counts."""
    _require_backend(backend)

    failed = all_runs_df[~all_runs_df["has_output"].astype(bool)].copy()
    if failed.empty:
        raise ValueError("No failed runs to plot")

    counts = failed["failure_reason"].value_counts().reset_index()
    counts.columns = ["failure_reason", "count"]

    n_fail = len(failed)
    n_total = len(all_runs_df)
    default_title = f"Failure Mode Distribution ({n_fail}/{n_total} failed)"

    if backend == "seaborn":
        sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, max(3, len(counts) * 0.8 + 1)))
        colors = sns.color_palette("Reds_r", n_colors=len(counts))
        sns.barplot(data=counts, x="count", y="failure_reason", palette=colors,
                    ax=ax, edgecolor="white")
        ax.set_xlabel("Number of Runs")
        ax.set_ylabel("")
        ax.set_title(title or default_title)
        for container in ax.containers:
            ax.bar_label(container, fmt="%d", fontsize=11, padding=5)
        ax.set_xlim(0, counts["count"].max() + 1.5)
        return fig

    fig = px.bar(
        counts, x="count", y="failure_reason", orientation="h",
        title=title or default_title,
        labels={"count": "Number of Runs", "failure_reason": ""},
        color="failure_reason",
        color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Set1,
        text="count",
    )
    fig.update_traces(textposition="outside")
    fig.update_layout(
        showlegend=False,
        height=max(300, len(counts) * 50 + 100),
        template="plotly_white",
        xaxis_range=[0, counts["count"].max() + 1.5],
    )
    return fig


def plot_failure_sunburst(
    all_runs_df: pd.DataFrame,
    backend: str = "seaborn",
    title: str | None = None,
    row_col: str = "model",
    col_col: str = "context",
):
    """Sunburst (plotly) or grouped bar (seaborn) of failure breakdown."""
    _require_backend(backend)

    failed = all_runs_df[~all_runs_df["has_output"].astype(bool)].copy()
    if failed.empty:
        raise ValueError("No failed runs to plot")

    n_fail = len(failed)

    if backend == "seaborn":
        counts = (

            .size()
            .reset_index(name="count")

        sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, max(4, len(counts) * 0.5 + 2)))

        ax.set_title(title or default_title)
        ax.set_xlabel("Number of Runs")
        ax.set_ylabel("")

    records = [
        {"failure_reason": r["failure_reason"], row_col: r[row_col],
         col_col: r[col_col], "count": 1}
        for _, r in failed.iterrows()
    ]
    df = pd.DataFrame(records)
    fig = px.sunburst(
        df, path=["failure_reason", row_col, col_col], values="count",
        title=title or default_title,

        color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Set2,

def plot_error_breakdown(
    runs_df: pd.DataFrame,
    backend: str = "seaborn",
    title: str | None = None,
    x_col: str = "display_label",
):
    """Stacked bar chart: hallucinations / omissions / genuine errors per run.

    Accepts either total counts (``total_hallucinations``,
    ``total_omissions``, ``total_genuine_errors``) or rates
    (``avg_hallucination_rate``, ``avg_omission_rate``) as fallback.
    """
    _require_backend(backend)

    total_types = ["total_hallucinations", "total_omissions", "total_genuine_errors"]
    rate_types = ["avg_hallucination_rate", "avg_omission_rate"]

    available_totals = [c for c in total_types if c in runs_df.columns]
    available_rates = [c for c in rate_types if c in runs_df.columns]

    use_rates = False
    if available_totals:
        available = available_totals
    elif available_rates:
        available = available_rates
        use_rates = True
    else:
        raise ValueError("No error breakdown columns found in runs data")

    data = runs_df.dropna(subset=available, how="all").copy()
    if data.empty:
        raise ValueError("No runs with error breakdown data")

    long_rows = []
    for _, row in data.iterrows():
        label = row.get(x_col, row.get("run_id", "unknown"))
        for etype in available:
            val = row.get(etype)
            if pd.notna(val):
                nice_name = (
                    etype.replace("total_", "")
                    .replace("avg_", "")
                    .replace("_rate", "")
                    .replace("_", " ")
                    .title()
                )
                value = float(val) if use_rates else int(val)
                long_rows.append({"run": label, "error_type": nice_name, "count": value})

    if not long_rows:
        raise ValueError("No error breakdown data to plot")

    edf = pd.DataFrame(long_rows)
    if use_rates:
        default_title = "Error Rates (Hallucination / Omission)"
    else:
        default_title = "Error Breakdown (Hallucinations / Omissions / Genuine Errors)"

    color_map = {
        "Hallucinations": "#e74c3c",
        "Hallucination": "#e74c3c",
        "Omissions": "#f39c12",
        "Omission": "#f39c12",
        "Genuine Errors": "#8e44ad",
        "Genuine": "#8e44ad",
    }
    canonical_order = ["Hallucinations", "Hallucination", "Omissions", "Omission",
                       "Genuine Errors", "Genuine"]

    if backend == "seaborn":
        sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
        pivot = edf.pivot_table(index="run", columns="error_type", values="count", fill_value=0)
        ordered_cols = [c for c in canonical_order if c in pivot.columns]
        pivot = pivot[ordered_cols]

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(8, len(pivot) * 1.5 + 2), 6))
        pivot.plot.bar(stacked=True, ax=ax, color=[color_map.get(c, "#999") for c in ordered_cols],
                       edgecolor="white")
        ax.set_title(title or default_title)
        ax.set_ylabel("Rate" if use_rates else "Count")
        ax.set_xlabel("")

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Harmonia Experiment SBATCH Template - CPU (Cloud LLM providers)
# =============================================================================
# This template is used by generate_jobs.py to create individual job scripts.
# Variables in {{double_braces}} are replaced by the generator.
#
# Usage:
#   sbatch jobs/experiment_gpt4o.sh
#
# Or generate jobs first:
#   python generate_jobs.py --config experiments/configs/dou_harmonization.yaml
#
# Note: For local LLM providers (ollama, anyllm:ollama), use sbatch_template_gpu.sh
#       or exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh will auto-start Ollama on CPU nodes too.
# =============================================================================

#SBATCH --job-name=harmonia_{{experiment_name}}
#SBATCH --output=/dev/null
#SBATCH --error=/dev/null
#SBATCH --time={{time_limit}}
#SBATCH --mem={{memory}}
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={{cpus}}
#SBATCH --gres=tmpspace:{{tmpspace}}G

# =============================================================================
# Environment Setup
# =============================================================================

set -e

# Generate unique run ID for linking logs to results
RUN_ID=$(python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(4))")
export RUN_ID
TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
RUN_RESULTS_DIR="{{project_dir}}/results/${TIMESTAMP}_{{experiment_name}}_${SLURM_JOB_ID}_${RUN_ID}"

# Redirect all output to date-stamped log files (includes run_id)
LOG_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%d-%m-%Y_%H%M)
LOG_OUT="logs/${LOG_TIMESTAMP}_{{experiment_name}}_${SLURM_JOB_ID}_${RUN_ID}.out"
LOG_ERR="logs/${LOG_TIMESTAMP}_{{experiment_name}}_${SLURM_JOB_ID}_${RUN_ID}.err"
mkdir -p logs
exec > "$LOG_OUT" 2> "$LOG_ERR"

echo "=============================================="
echo "Harmonia Experiment: {{experiment_name}}"
echo "=============================================="
echo ""
echo "Job ID: $SLURM_JOB_ID"
echo "Run ID: $RUN_ID"
echo "Node: $(hostname)"
echo "Date: $(date)"
echo ""

# Change to project directory
cd {{project_dir}}

# Dynamic port based on job ID to avoid conflicts
PORT=$((8100 + (SLURM_JOB_ID % 100)))
echo "Using port: $PORT"

# Create logs directory
mkdir -p logs

# =============================================================================
# Start Beaker Server with exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh
# =============================================================================
# The exec script handles:
# - Ollama auto-start for local LLM providers (ollama, anyllm:ollama)
# - Ollama logging to logs/ollama_<timestamp>.log
# - Model pre-loading/warming
# - Apptainer image selection (new harmonia image with litellm support)
# - Data and results directory binding
# - Environment variable configuration

echo ""
echo "Starting Beaker server on port $PORT..."
echo "LLM Provider: {{llm_provider}}"
echo "LLM Model: {{llm_model}}"
echo ""

# Start Beaker server via exec script (handles Ollama automatically if needed)
./exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh \
    --port $PORT \
    --config {{config_path}} \
    --job-name "{{experiment_name}}_${SLURM_JOB_ID}" \
    --results-dir "$RUN_RESULTS_DIR" \
    --run-id "$RUN_ID" &

SERVER_PID=$!
echo "Server PID: $SERVER_PID"

# Function to cleanup on exit
cleanup() {
    echo ""
    echo "Cleaning up..."
    if [ -n "$SERVER_PID" ]; then
        kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true
        wait $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    echo "Done."
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for server to be ready
echo "Waiting for server to start..."
MAX_WAIT=90  # Increased timeout for potential model loading
WAITED=0
while [ $WAITED -lt $MAX_WAIT ]; do
    if curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:$PORT/api" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "200\|401"; then
        echo "Server is ready!"
        break
    fi
    sleep 2
    WAITED=$((WAITED + 2))
    echo "  Waiting... ($WAITED/$MAX_WAIT seconds)"
done

if [ $WAITED -ge $MAX_WAIT ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Server failed to start within $MAX_WAIT seconds"
    exit 1
fi

# =============================================================================
# Run Experiment
# =============================================================================

echo ""
echo "Running experiment..."
echo "Config: {{config_path}}"
echo ""

# Get token from env file
TOKEN=$(grep "^JUPYTER_TOKEN=" {{env_file}} | cut -d '=' -f2)

# Run the experiment
.venv/bin/python run_experiment.py \
    --config {{config_path}} \
    --server http://localhost:$PORT \
    --token "$TOKEN" \
    --timeout {{timeout}}

EXIT_CODE=$?

# =============================================================================
# Completion
# =============================================================================

echo ""
echo "=============================================="
if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Experiment completed successfully!"
else
    echo "Experiment failed with exit code: $EXIT_CODE"
fi
echo "=============================================="

exit $EXIT_CODE
